slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, open each automation tool mentioned (Flow Builder, the legacy Process Builder/Workflow Rules entries if present, Approval Processes) and write down, for each one, one real business rule from a company you know that it could enforce.
slots.deliverable: A written list mapping each Salesforce automation tool to one real-world business rule it could enforce.

slots.practicalActivity: In your Trailhead Playground or Developer Edition org, open Flow Builder from Setup, start a new flow, and tour the canvas, the Toolbox (Elements/Resources/Manager tabs), and the Run/Debug/Save buttons without building anything yet.
slots.deliverable: A written list of the Toolbox's 3 tabs and what each one is for, based on your own tour of Flow Builder.

slots.practicalActivity: Start a new Screen Flow named Flow Basics Practice and, using only the Toolbox Resources tab, create one Variable, one Formula, and one Constant resource, giving each a realistic API name.
slots.deliverable: One saved (not necessarily activated) flow containing a Variable, a Formula, and a Constant resource.

slots.practicalActivity: In Flow Basics Practice, write a Formula resource that combines two of your Variables (for example concatenating a first and last name variable), and confirm the formula's data type is set correctly.
slots.deliverable: One Formula resource in your flow that correctly references and combines 2 existing Variables.

slots.practicalActivity: In Flow Basics Practice, create a record variable of type Account, and a second variable of type Text, Number, and Date/Time each, confirming Flow Builder's object picker and data-type picker for each.
slots.deliverable: One record variable (Account) plus 3 primitive-type variables, all visible in the flow's Resources list.

slots.practicalActivity: Without further instructions, rebuild Flow Basics Practice from scratch under a new name, choosing a different object and a different mix of resource types than before, to confirm you can set up variables, constants, and formulas independently.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently built flow containing at least one Variable, one Constant, and one Formula resource on a different object.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a before-save, record-triggered flow on Case: when Category changes to "Outage", set Priority to "High" using Fast Field Updates. Debug it against a test Case to confirm Priority updates without a second save.
slots.deliverable: One activated before-save flow on Case that sets Priority to High when Category equals Outage.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an after-save, record-triggered flow on Opportunity that sends an Email Alert when Stage changes to Closed Won, and explain in writing why this requirement could not have been done as a before-save flow.
slots.deliverable: One activated after-save flow on Opportunity triggering an email action, plus a written explanation of why after-save was required.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a screen flow with 2 screens: the first collects a Text input and a Picklist choice, the second displays a Display Text confirmation referencing both values back to the user.
slots.deliverable: One runnable screen flow with 2 screens, where the second screen echoes back data collected on the first.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Schedule-Triggered Flow that runs daily against Task records, using Get Records to find open Tasks past their due date, without yet acting on them (that comes in Lesson 16-17).
slots.deliverable: One scheduled flow configured to run daily, with a Get Records element that finds overdue open Tasks.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a simple Autolaunched Flow (no trigger, no screen) that accepts one input variable and one output variable, performing a basic Assignment between them, so it is ready to be called by another flow.
slots.deliverable: One autolaunched flow with a defined input and output variable, ready to be invoked as a subflow.

slots.practicalActivity: From your screen flow built in Lesson 8, add a Subflow element that calls the autolaunched flow from Lesson 10, mapping the screen's collected input into the subflow's input variable and displaying its output on a final screen.
slots.deliverable: One screen flow that calls your autolaunched flow as a subflow and displays its returned output.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a simple custom Platform Event object in Setup, then build a Platform Event-Triggered Flow that starts when that event is received and writes a Display Text-free log by creating a record capturing the event's payload fields.
slots.deliverable: One custom Platform Event definition and one flow that triggers on it and records the event's data.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently build a second mini-automation chain combining 2 different flow types from this chapter (for example a scheduled flow that calls an autolaunched subflow), choosing the business scenario yourself.
slots.deliverable: A second original automation combining 2 distinct flow types from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page comparison chart of all 7 flow types covered in this chapter (trigger, typical use case, whether it can use a screen), and check it against every flow you built in Chapter 2.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison chart of the 7 flow types, cross-checked against your own built flows.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Decision element named Check Case Details on a Case-based flow with outcomes for Severity 0 through Severity 2 plus a relabeled Default (Severity 3), each with its own condition on Case Type, and confirm outcome order determines which path a record with multiple matching conditions actually takes.
slots.deliverable: One Decision element with 4 ordered outcomes, tested against a record that could match more than one outcome.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a flow that uses Get Records to retrieve an Opportunity's related Opportunity Line Items into a collection, then a Loop element that iterates over the collection accumulating the total quantity into a running-total variable.
slots.deliverable: One flow with a Loop element that correctly totals a numeric field across a collection of child records.

slots.practicalActivity: In the same flow, inspect the collection variable's properties to confirm it is correctly flagged as a collection of records, then add a second collection variable storing just the Contact Ids extracted during the loop.
slots.deliverable: A flow containing 2 distinct collection variables, one of full records and one of extracted Ids.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure a Get Records element with 2 filter conditions combined with AND, sort the results, and set it to return all matching records into a collection rather than just the first.
slots.deliverable: One Get Records element with 2 combined filters, sorting, and an all-records (collection) output configured.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the Opportunity flow to Create a related Task record, Update the parent Opportunity with a rollup field you calculated in the loop, and add a separate branch that Deletes a stale test record, confirming each DML element's result.
slots.deliverable: One flow using Create Records, Update Records, and Delete Records elements, each verified against real data.

slots.practicalActivity: Review every Assignment element used in this chapter's flows so far and confirm each one uses the correct operator (Assign, Add, Subtract) for what it's actually doing, correcting any that default to the wrong operator.
slots.deliverable: A written audit confirming the Assignment operator used in each flow built this chapter is correct for its purpose.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Transform element that reshapes your Opportunity Line Item collection into a simpler collection containing only Product Name and Line Total, mapped field-by-field.
slots.deliverable: One Transform element that produces a reshaped collection containing only the 2 mapped fields.

slots.practicalActivity: On a different object than Opportunity, independently build a flow using a Decision, a Loop over a collection retrieved with Get Records, and at least one Create, Update, or Delete Records element, choosing the scenario yourself.
slots.deliverable: A second original flow on a new object combining Decision, Loop, and a DML element.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk through every flow-logic flow built this chapter and write a short note on where bulkification could be a concern (a Get Records or DML element inside a loop), flagging anything you'd want to move outside the loop.
slots.deliverable: A written bulkification review flagging any in-loop Get Records or DML elements across this chapter's flows.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a fault path to one of your earlier DML elements (for example the Create Records Task step) that captures {!$Flow.FaultMessage} and either displays it on a screen (if the flow has one) or writes it to a field on the record.
slots.deliverable: One flow with a working fault path that captures and surfaces the real $Flow.FaultMessage value.

slots.practicalActivity: Use Flow Builder's Debug feature on 3 of your earlier flows, supplying realistic sample input values each time, and read the debug trace to confirm which path each element actually took.
slots.deliverable: 3 completed debug runs with sample inputs, each with a written note on the path the debug trace showed.

slots.practicalActivity: Take the bulkification review you wrote in Chapter 3 and actually fix one flow: move its in-loop Get Records or DML element outside the loop so it runs once against a collection instead of once per iteration.
slots.deliverable: One flow refactored so a Get Records or DML element that was inside a loop now runs once, outside it.

slots.practicalActivity: Run your refactored flow's debug trace again and locate the governor-limit usage (SOQL queries, DML statements) shown, comparing it to the same flow's usage before the bulkification fix.
slots.deliverable: A written before/after comparison of governor-limit usage for one flow, from its debug trace.

slots.practicalActivity: Save a new version of one of your activated flows with a small change, confirm both versions appear in the flow's version list, activate the new version, and confirm the old version is now inactive but retained.
slots.deliverable: One flow with 2 saved versions, the newer one active and the older one retained but inactive.

slots.practicalActivity: If Flow Orchestration is available in your org, open Orchestrator Builder and sketch a 2-stage orchestration (for example a submit stage then a review stage) using 2 of your existing flows as stage steps; otherwise, write the same 2-stage design as a document.
slots.deliverable: A 2-stage Orchestration (built or documented) that sequences 2 of your existing flows.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one flow you have not yet hardened and independently add a fault path, confirm it bulk-safe through debug, and save a second version of it, applying every reliability technique from this chapter without step-by-step guidance.
slots.deliverable: One previously unhardened flow now with a fault path, confirmed bulk-safe, and saved as a second version.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a flow health-check checklist covering fault handling, bulkification, governor limits, and versioning, then run every flow you have built so far in this course against it, noting any gaps found.
slots.deliverable: A written flow health-check checklist applied to every flow built so far, with any gaps noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch an automation architecture diagram for a fictional company's Lead-to-Opportunity process, deciding which parts should be before-save flows, after-save flows, screen flows, or subflows, and justify each choice in writing.
slots.deliverable: A written or diagrammed automation architecture for a Lead-to-Opportunity process, with a justification for each flow-type choice.

slots.practicalActivity: Adopt an Object - Trigger Context - Purpose naming convention and rename every flow you have built in this course to follow it, adding a one-sentence description to each flow's properties.
slots.deliverable: Every flow built so far in this course renamed to a consistent convention, each with a written description.

lessons.title: Migrating From Process Builder and Workflow Rules

slots.practicalActivity: If your org has any legacy Workflow Rules or Process Builder processes (Setup > Process Automation), open one and rebuild its logic as an equivalent record-triggered flow; if none exist, design one on paper (field updates plus one email action) and rebuild that as a flow.
slots.deliverable: One record-triggered flow that replicates a real or paper-designed legacy Workflow Rule/Process Builder process.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the lab's before-save Lead - Before Save - Owner Assignment flow exactly as designed: a Territory_Assignment__c custom object, a Get Records lookup by State, a Decision on whether a match was found, 2 Assignment paths (matched owner vs. fallback queue), and a fault path writing the error to a Lead_Assignment_Error__c field, then debug it with a matching and a non-matching State.
slots.deliverable: One activated before-save Lead flow with territory lookup, fallback assignment, and a field-based fault path, debugged against both a matching and a non-matching case.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the lab's Case escalation flow as designed: a scheduled or record-triggered flow that checks Case age/SLA against a Decision, escalates matching Cases by reassigning Owner and raising Priority, and logs any lookup fault to a field on the Case, debugged with an escalating and a non-escalating test Case.
slots.deliverable: One activated Case escalation flow, debugged against both an escalating and a non-escalating test Case.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the lab's multi-screen onboarding wizard screen flow as designed: an input screen collecting new-hire details, a Decision branching by role, a subflow call provisioning role-specific records, and a final confirmation screen, run end to end as a real user would.
slots.deliverable: One completed, runnable onboarding wizard screen flow taken end to end as a test user, producing the expected provisioned records.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine all 3 practice-lab flows (Lead Assignment, Case Escalation, Onboarding Wizard) into a single demo: trigger each one with realistic test data in sequence, capturing the before/after state of every record each flow touches, with no lesson-by-lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: A single end-to-end demo run of all 3 practice-lab flows against real test data, with before/after record states documented for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a final course portfolio summary covering every flow built across all 5 chapters: its type, its business purpose, how it handles faults and bulk safety, and how it is named and documented, as if handing your whole flow library off to another admin.
slots.deliverable: A final written portfolio summary of every flow built in this course, organized by chapter, serving as a handoff document.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design and build production-ready Salesforce Flows end to end: choosing the right flow type (record-triggered, screen, scheduled, autolaunched, platform-event, or subflow), using decisions, loops, collections and record elements correctly, adding fault handling and bulk-safe performance, and deploying flows with proper versioning, naming conventions and documentation.
